R0070.title: Automated Reselling
R0070.definition: Using automated means to automatically purchase and resell goods through a platform's normal transaction process.
R0070.description: Automated reselling typically serves three purposes: first, buying low and selling high to profit from price differences; second, listing products without actual stock and fulfilling orders through other stocked stores; third, using automation to bulk-create store clusters for mass product listing.
R0070.influence: Buy-low-sell-high behavior, once discovered by users, creates the impression of inflated prices on the platform, causing reputational damage and user churn; dropshipping stores often negate competitive advantages or lead to unfair competition; store clusters occupy large amounts of search and recommendation resources, leading to unfair competition.

observables: Newly listed products are snatched and ordered within seconds by the same cohort of accounts, with a highly mechanical purchase timing pattern
Stores or account matrices bulk-list identical products with abnormally high listing concentration and anomalous pricing
Shipping addresses or payment accounts recur across platforms, exhibiting cross-platform dropshipping and forwarding patterns
Specific stores surge in exposure within paid search ranking results and are priced significantly higher than comparable offerings

R0070-001.title: Buy Low, Sell High
R0070-001.definition: Selling products from other platforms or stores at a higher price on the current platform or store to profit from the price difference.
R0070-001.description: A typical buy-low-sell-high approach involves significantly marking up a product's price and then using search bidding ranking mechanisms to place the product at the top of results for greater exposure. Black-market actors use automation to monitor cross-platform price gaps and bulk-forward low-price inventory to this platform for high-price resale, profiting from the spread while creating the illusion of inflated platform prices, squeezing legitimate seller exposure and driving user churn.
R0070-001.influence: This behavior creates the impression of inflated prices on the platform for users, leading to user churn.

observables: The same product is priced significantly higher on this platform than on others, and the listing secures top exposure through paid ranking
Store product prices are inflated and sales concentrate on high-exposure search slots, with abnormal conversion rates
Cross-platform price-comparison data is scraped in bulk and used to set the markup magnitude on this platform
The same seller operates the same product across multiple platforms, with systematically higher pricing on this platform

R0070-002.title: Dropshipping Store
R0070-002.definition: Listing products from other platforms or stores on the current platform or store, and placing orders through the original stocked store when a user places an order.
R0070-002.description: Buy-low-sell-high (R0070-001) is generally also a form of dropshipping, but buy-low-sell-high is more focused on gaining exposure, while dropshipping is more focused on gaining order volume. For example, if a seller only has a store on Platform A and not on Platform B, Platform A gains a competitive advantage. But if the seller lists products on Platform B and fulfills orders through Platform A when users order on B, this competitive advantage is negated — especially if Platform B subsidizes the originally unstocked products, creating the illusion that Platform B is always cheaper than Platform A.
R0070-002.influence: Cross-platform dropshipping reduces the competitive advantage of the original platform and may lead to unfair competition, causing financial or reputational losses.

references.title: Can You Really Sell Without Inventory? Risks of 'Effortless' Online Stores - Beijing Chaoyang District Government

observables: After orders are placed on this platform, the order details are synced to stocked stores on other platforms for fulfillment, with tracking numbers reused across platforms
A store has no own inventory yet continuously takes orders, and its shipping addresses do not match the store's registered entity
The same product is priced systematically lower on this platform than on the source platform, exhibiting subsidy-arbitrage characteristics
The store's listing refresh cadence is highly synchronized with changes to external platforms' product catalogs

R0070-003.title: Store Cluster
R0070-003.definition: May be a form of dropshipping store (R0070-002) or may have actual stock. Typically refers to bulk-creating stores to increase exposure.
R0070-003.description: By bulk-creating large numbers of stores to increase exposure and expand the display area of products or services, attracting more potential customers. This practice is typically aimed at increasing product or service visibility on the platform, improving exposure in search results, and gaining more traffic and sales opportunities.
R0070-003.influence: Occupies display opportunities of other stores on the platform, and the mass listing of similar products makes it harder for users to discover differentiated products.

observables: The same entity or device bulk-registers large numbers of stores, with highly correlated qualifications, legal representatives, or contact information
Stores in the cluster list identical products with high listing concentration and near-identical titles and images
Search results are dominated by stores from the same matrix, squeezing out the exposure of other stores
Stores in the cluster list and delist products in lockstep, with operational actions showing unified scheduling
